opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles — up 57% YoY as Tesla builds out its AI compute and robotaxi infrastructure.

opex.note: Restructuring and other one-off operating charges.

footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $1,389M; $1,373M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: $6.2B of operating cash flow less $2.2B of capex

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $238M sit inside operating expenses (vs $55M a year ago), and stock-based compensation was $663M — a non-cash cost inside the expense lines.

Other income includes an $80M gain on digital assets (Tesla's bitcoin holdings are marked to market each quarter). Excluding stock pay and digital-asset moves, non-GAAP net income was $1,770M ($0.50 a share) vs GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders of $1,373M ($0.39).
otherDetail: Interest income of $439M, less $76M of interest expense and $28M of other expense, net — a net +$335M below operating profit.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Car sales, leasing and regulatory credits — up 6% YoY on record deliveries of 497,099, with regulatory credit revenue of $417M vs $739M a year ago.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack battery systems and solar — up 44% YoY on record storage deployments of 12.5 GWh.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, service centers, parts and FSD (supervised-driving) subscriptions — up 25% YoY.

takeaways.text: Tesla delivered 497,099 vehicles — its best quarter ever, up 7% YoY — and deployed a record 12.5 GWh of energy storage, up 81%, as buyers pulled purchases forward before the U.S. EV tax credit expired.
takeaways.title: A record quarter for volume

takeaways.text: Operating income dropped 40% YoY to $1,624M: price cuts and a higher average cost per vehicle (tariffs included) squeezed gross margin to 18.0%, while operating expenses jumped 50% on AI and R&D spending.
takeaways.title: Profit fell anyway

takeaways.text: Free cash flow hit a record $3,990M — $6,238M of operating cash flow less $2,248M of capex — lifting cash and investments to $41.6B.
takeaways.title: Record free cash flow

verdict: Tesla delivered a record 497,099 cars and grew revenue 12% to $28.1B, but price cuts, tariff costs and a 50% jump in operating expenses — AI spending above all — cut operating income 40% to $1.6B.
